model_availability_probe.method: One trivial prompt per model, no tools: `claude -p --model <id>` (Claude Code 2.1.299) and `codex exec --model <id> -c model_reasoning_effort=medium` (codex-cli 0.159.3, host). All 4 Claude and all 9 listed Codex ids returned 'ok'. Models are entered in the order above so that any partial run still contains both families early.

per_model_schedule: Each model runs the same 36 cells: 6 tasks x 3 arms x 2 repetitions. Phase 1 = the 24 arm A and arm C cells, built in (repetition, task, arm A then C) order and shuffled with random.Random(seed); phase 2 = the 12 arm B cells, built in (repetition, task) order and shuffled with random.Random(seed + 1), run after phase 1 because B reviews and fixes THAT model's own arm A deliverable of the same task and repetition. One model call at a time across the entire campaign; models run one after another in the order above.
arm_B_input: The same model's own arm A deliverable (final-artifacts/<task>-official-generator-r<rep>/tests/) from this run, copied into a fresh baseline project as untracked files. If that A cell has no spec file, the B cell is UNAVAILABLE (no call) and scores 0 like its A cell.

transports.codex: The pilot container adapter (generator_codex_official_adapter.py, unchanged): codex-cli 0.159.3 in the pinned Docker image, `--model <id>`, model_reasoning_effort=medium, same prompts as the pilots. Arm A uses `init-agents --loop=codex` and the frozen toml digests of generator-official-pilot-v1.
transports.claude: generator_claude_multimodel_adapter.py: Claude Code 2.1.299 `claude -p` on the host, `--model <id> --effort medium --output-format stream-json --json-schema`, max budget 30 USD as a safety cap only. Skill isolation: `--disable-slash-commands` plus `--strict-mcp-config` on every call, and the runner verifies the system/init event of every call (skills list empty; official playwright agents and the playwright-test MCP server visible only in arm A; no web tools; Write/Edit absent for the arm A parent and present for arms B and C); a violating call is an infrastructure error, never data. The official generator definition pins `model: sonnet` in its frontmatter, which a pre-freeze preflight showed overrides CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL (the subagent ran on claude-sonnet-5-5 under a haiku parent). After the digest check, the runner therefore replaces exactly that one line with `model: inherit` in the staged copy (nothing else in the definition changes) and also sets CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL for the general-purpose subagents of arms B and C; every Claude cell reports modelUsage, and cells whose modelUsage names any other model are counted (cells_with_other_models_used). Tool scope: arm A parent Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Agent plus the `playwright-test` MCP tools from the project's `.mcp.json` (project settings source only, so `.claude/agents/*.md` from `init-agents --loop=claude` load); arms B and C Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Write, Edit, Agent, no settings source, no MCP. A deny list blocks Read of the repository's skills/benchmarks/docs, sibling benchmark worktrees and the saved evidence directories; Bash is not path-restricted, so every call is audited afterward (compliance.home_paths_touched_outside_work).

metrics.cost_comparability: Codex and Claude token counts and wall times are not comparable across families (different tokenizers, caching, tool loops); they are compared within a family and shown across families only as raw numbers.

decision.no_p_values: DESCRIPTIVE ONLY. No confidence interval, no significance claim, no PASS/FAIL release verdict.
decision.per_model_label: For each model with all 36 cells scored and each contrast X vs Y: the contrast is EVALUABLE for that model only if both arms delivered at least one spec file in at least 6 of their 12 cells (an arm the model could not drive is a harness-compatibility result, not a quality difference; it is reported as-run in the tables but never turned into a label). If evaluable: 'suggestive: X better' if the per-task refactor survival (mean of 2 repetitions) has the same sign for X in at least 5 of the 6 tasks AND for X the clean-3/3 rate, effective fault kill, scanner P0 total and scanner P1/P2 total are each not worse than for Y (<= for scanner totals); symmetric for Y; otherwise 'nothing'. Ties and 3-3 splits are 'nothing'. Same rule as both pilots (min_tasks_same_sign = 5). Otherwise the label is 'not evaluable'.
decision.cross_model_consistency: Per contrast, let N be the number of complete models for which that contrast is evaluable. The contrast is 'replicated across models' only if N >= 4 and (a) at least ceil(2N/3) of those models carry the same 'suggestive: X better' label, (b) none of them carries the opposite suggestive label, and (c) the agreeing models include at least one Claude-family and one Codex-family model. If N < 4 the verdict is 'not evaluable'; otherwise 'not replicated' with the exact counts. No intermediate wording such as 'partly replicated' is used.
decision.incomplete_models: A model that is stopped (usage limit, disk, repeated infrastructure failure) before 36 cells are scored is listed as incomplete, shown descriptively, and excluded from the labels and from N.
decision.pooled_view: Descriptive only: per-arm means across complete models and per-task sign counts of the pooled model-level differences; it never substitutes for the rule above.
decision.reference_row: gpt-5.5 from the two pilots is printed as a reference row, never part of N.

stop_rules: One model call at a time across the whole campaign; load pause at 1-min load average > 40 (up to 1800 s per wait).

Stop the whole campaign when free disk on the work volume is below 4 GiB (4294967296 bytes), before every call and before every scoring cell batch; resume with `drive --allow-live` (resumes every model from its saved final.json).
Stop on a usage/rate limit or any digest drift.

A cell whose call is an infrastructure error after the inherited single retry is retried again at most twice by later resumes; after that it stays a recorded infrastructure failure, scores 0 as-run, and the campaign continues. Three consecutive infrastructure-error cells stop the campaign.
Never edit this protocol, the runners, adapters or freeze after the first scheduled call; a change needs a successor protocol.
limits: 6 task clusters x 2 repetitions per arm per model: tiny, descriptive only. The 6 tasks are the same synthetic fixtures as the pilots, author-written faults, one refactor per task.

Arm A and arm C are not the same agent loop on Claude and Codex: the official generator is a host-specific subagent loop (`--loop=claude` vs `--loop=codex`) and arm A's Claude parent has no Write/Edit tools by design; the Codex arm A parent keeps its default tools and is only instructed not to write specs. This asymmetry is intentional (mechanical enforcement of 'the agent writes the spec') and is a confound across families.

Claude runs on the host (real browser, no container); Codex runs in the pinned Linux container. Claude Bash is not path-sandboxed; only a Read deny list and an after-the-fact audit protect against reading the saved evidence.
Arm B reviews the same model's own arm A output, so B and A cells are not independent; arm B fixes are written by a model that also wrote the code.
Models are run on different days and times: host load and provider-side drift are not controlled. Model identifiers are what the local CLI accepted; they are provenance, not attestation.
Parent token usage excludes child agents for Codex; Claude session totals include subagents. Not comparable across families.
The 2.0.1 skills are the pilots' skills; nothing here is a release claim.
